prompt.context: Your client, Minty Fresh Co., has been the dominant leader in Oral Mouthwash for over a century since inventing a unique four oil combination that kills 99% of germs and leaves consumers with a 'dentist fresh' clean feeling. Minty Fresh has consistently held 80–90% of the market share for mouthwash, but in the last 3 years, share and profit has been rapidly declining. Your client, the CEO of the US division, has hired you to determine what is driving the decline and how to quickly reverse this trend.
prompt.question: What is driving Minty Fresh's declining share and profit, and how can the company quickly reverse this trend?

clarifying_info.q: Are we focused only on the US market?
clarifying_info.a: Yes, this case is only focused on US sales; global impact is ignored.

clarifying_info.q: What time period are we working in?
clarifying_info.a: Assume it is January 2016. Results need to be achieved within the 11 remaining months of 2016.

clarifying_info.q: Does Minty Fresh sell products other than mouthwash?
clarifying_info.a: No, Minty Fresh only sells mouthwash, not other oral care products.

exhibits.title: US Mouthwash Landscape
exhibits.shows: A stacked bar chart showing revenues by company in the US mouthwash market for 2012–2015, broken out by Minty Fresh, Clean B, Sparkle, and Other.

exhibits.title: Competitive Pricing
exhibits.shows: Two sections: (1) a bar chart of list prices by bottle size for Minty Fresh, Clean B, and Sparkle; (2) a table of Minty Fresh's 2015 list price and volume by bottle size.

data.list_prices_bar_chart: Minty Fresh, Clean B, and Sparkle prices shown for 250ML, 500ML, 1L, and 1.5L bottles (values readable from chart)

framework: Revenue and profit decomposition: revenue = price x volume; probe both dimensions
Competitive landscape: who is taking share and why
Market sizing: category growth vs. share shift
Pricing strategy: price positioning relative to competitors by SKU
Volume drivers: new products, buy-rate increases, new retail channels
Implementation constraints: timeline (11 months remaining in 2016), retailer contracts, supply chain

questions.prompt: After reviewing Exhibit 1, what are the key observations about the competitive landscape?
questions.guidance: Interviewee should identify: (1) Minty Fresh is declining in both share and absolute revenue; (2) two new competitors, Clean B and Sparkle, have rapidly taken share over the last 3 years; (3) total category revenue is relatively flat (~$1B–$1.1B), so this is a share-stealing dynamic, not category growth. Current 2015 share: 770/1100 = ~70%.

math.setup: Minty Fresh 2015 revenue = $770M; total category = $1,100M; share = 770/1100
math.answer: Minty Fresh holds approximately 70% share in 2015, down from ~90% in 2012

questions.prompt: Assuming the category remains flat, what incremental revenue does Minty Fresh need to grow market share by 3 percentage points in 2016?
questions.guidance: Category is flat at ~$1,100M. A 3 pp increase from 70% to 73% share equals 3% of $1,100M = $33M incremental revenue. This $33M figure is used as the target throughout the rest of the case.

math.setup: Category total = $1,100M (flat); current share = 70%; target share = 73%; incremental share = 3 pp

questions.prompt: What strategies should Minty Fresh consider to quickly regain share?
questions.guidance: A strong answer uses a marketing/revenue framework covering price and volume levers. Volume levers: (1) new product launches, (2) increase buy rate of current users, (3) expand to new retail channels (gas stations, beauty stores). Price levers: increase or decrease prices by SKU. A good interviewee recognizes the 11-month time constraint and concludes that new product launches and new retail distribution are slow to execute, making pricing the quickest actionable lever for 2016.

questions.prompt: After reviewing Exhibit 2, what pricing opportunities exist for Minty Fresh?
questions.guidance: Interviewee should observe: (1) Minty Fresh is underpriced vs. competitors in 250ML and 500ML — opportunity to raise prices; (2) Minty Fresh is overpriced in 1L and 1.5L — opportunity to lower prices to drive volume; (3) A good interviewee mentions price elasticity and how it affects net revenue impact. They may also note that 1L and 1.5L are higher-volume SKUs and thus have greater revenue impact from price changes.

questions.prompt: Using the elasticity data below and Exhibit 2 volume/price data, calculate whether Minty Fresh can hit the $33M incremental revenue target. Elasticity assumptions: 250ML — 20% price increase drives 10% volume decrease; 500ML — 15% price increase drives 10% volume decrease; 1L — 20% price decrease drives 30% volume increase; 1.5L — 15% price decrease drives 20% volume increase.
questions.guidance: Interviewee should build a table tracking old price, new price, old volume, incremental volume, and change in revenue for each SKU. Total comes to ~$29.8M, close to the $33M target. Interviewee can recommend proceeding if they note ~$30M is close enough, or argue against if they defend the gap.

math.setup: Start from 2015 price and volume per SKU from Exhibit 2; apply elasticity assumptions
math.answer: ~$29.8M incremental revenue, approximately $3M short of the $33M target but close enough to move forward

questions.prompt: What factors would need to be considered before implementing a price change?
questions.guidance: Strong answers cover multiple stakeholder dimensions: (1) End consumers — reaction to price increases, potential volume loss exceeding estimates; (2) Retailers — contract terms, willingness to pass through price changes, shelf placement risk; (3) Internal supply chain — aligning production volumes with new demand projections (especially volume increases for 1L and 1.5L); (4) Profit impact — ensuring margin improvement net of volume changes; (5) Competitor reaction — risk of price war if competitors respond by cutting prices.

recommendation: Minty Fresh should implement a targeted pricing strategy across its four bottle sizes: raise prices on 250ML (+20%) and 500ML (+15%) where it is underpriced versus competitors, and lower prices on 1L (-20%) and 1.5L (-15%) to drive volume in its largest SKUs
This pricing action is projected to generate approximately $29.8M in incremental revenue, approaching the $33M target needed to grow share by 3 percentage points in 2016
Given the 11-month window, pricing is the fastest lever available — new product launches and new retail expansion cannot be executed in time
risks: Consumer backlash to price increases on 250ML and 500ML could exceed elasticity estimates
Retailers may resist implementing price changes or reduce shelf space
Competitors (Clean B, Sparkle) may retaliate with price cuts, triggering a price war that erodes margins
Volume increases for 1L and 1.5L may strain supply chain capacity
next_steps: Work with retailer partners to roll through price changes on agreed timelines
Align supply chain and production volumes with new demand projections, especially for 1L and 1.5L
Consider complementary marketing efforts (TV, digital) to support the pricing repositioning
Monitor competitor pricing responses closely and prepare contingency plans
Explore medium-term volume levers (new retail channels, buy-rate programs) for 2017 planning
